category: Acoustics Module II: thermoviscous acoustics, aeroacoustics, ultrasound, elastic and poroelastic waves, pipe acoustics
description: Microacoustics (thermoviscous FD/transient/boundary mode/SLNS), flow acoustics (linearized Euler, Navier-Stokes and potential flow, compressible potential flow, imported CGNS flow), time-explicit dG ultrasound and elastic-wave interfaces, Biot poroelastic waves and 1D pipe acoustics of the COMSOL Acoustics Module (6.x). Java type strings were read from the COMSOL 6.4 code-completion data and Application Library models.

tools.name: Thermoviscous Acoustics, Transient (tatd)
tools.description: Time-domain counterpart of Thermoviscous Acoustics, Frequency Domain: solves the linearized continuity, momentum and energy equations for acoustic pressure, velocity and temperature including viscous and thermal boundary-layer losses, for microacoustic devices (microphones, receivers, hearing aids, MEMS). Nonlinear effects such as vortex shedding at sudden expansions or high-SPL equation-of-state nonlinearity are added with Nonlinear Thermoviscous Acoustics Contributions, and moving-mesh coupling enables nonlinear squeeze-film damping. Available in 3D, 2D, 1D and 2D/1D axisymmetry with a scattered-field formulation.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Acoustics > Thermoviscous Acoustics > Thermoviscous Acoustics, Transient; Study > Time Dependent; set the maximum frequency in Transient Solver and Mesh Settings. Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("tatd", "ThermoacousticsSinglePhysicsTransient", "geom1")

parameters.name: Thermoviscous Acoustics Model (tam1)
parameters.description: Equilibrium p0/T0 model inputs and fluid properties mu, muB, kcond, Cp, rho0, alpha_p, betaT.

parameters.name: Wall (wall1)
parameters.description: Default no-slip isothermal wall; mechanical and thermal conditions combinable.

parameters.name: Transient Solver and Mesh Settings
parameters.description: Maximum frequency to resolve; tatd.d_visc/d_therm are evaluated at this frequency.

parameters.name: Nonlinear Thermoviscous Acoustics Contributions
parameters.description: Optional second-order terms.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module. Resolve the boundary layers with a boundary-layer mesh; the default discretization is P1 pressure with P2 velocity and temperature. Couple to pressure acoustics far from walls with the Acoustic-Thermoviscous Acoustic Boundary coupling (loudspeaker_driver_transient).

tools.name: Thermoviscous Acoustics, Boundary Mode (tabm)
tools.description: Boundary mode analysis on the cross section or inlet of a small duct that includes the viscous and thermal boundary-layer losses, solving for pressure, velocity and temperature mode shapes and the complex out-of-plane wave number kn. Used to set up sources and ports in small ducts of hearing aids and mobile devices and to identify propagation constants and characteristic impedances of lossy waveguides. Available on boundaries in 3D and 2D axisymmetry.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Acoustics > Thermoviscous Acoustics > Thermoviscous Acoustics, Boundary Mode; Study > Mode Analysis. Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("tabm", "ThermoacousticsBoundaryMode", "geom1")

parameters.name: Thermoviscous Acoustics Model
parameters.description: Fluid properties plus the propagation direction n of the modes (default the boundary normal).

parameters.name: Wall / No Slip / Isothermal / Adiabatic
parameters.description: Edge conditions around the cross section.

parameters.name: Mode Analysis study: modeFreq, neigs, shift
parameters.description: Frequency and number of modes; search around a wave number such as k0 = omega/c.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module. Check that alpha0 and betaT are not zero (material data errors are common). In/out-of-plane velocity variables are available for postprocessing.

tools.name: Thermoviscous Acoustics, SLNS Approximation (slns)
tools.description: Sequential Linearized Navier-Stokes (SLNS) interface that captures thermoviscous boundary-layer losses at a fraction of the cost of the full formulation by solving three scalar Helmholtz equations sequentially: the viscous and thermal scaling functions and the acoustic pressure. It is suited for large system models (ear simulators, couplers, phone acoustics) where the wavelength is much larger than the boundary-layer thickness, and generalizes Narrow Region Acoustics and the boundary-layer impedance to arbitrary geometry. Losses from redirectional flow at sudden expansions or perforates are not fully captured.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Acoustics > Thermoviscous Acoustics > Thermoviscous Acoustics, SLNS Approximation; Study > Frequency Domain. Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("slns", "ThermoviscousAcousticsSLNSApproximation", "geom1")

parameters.name: Thermoviscous Acoustics Model (tam1)
parameters.description: Fluid properties c, rho, mu, kcond, Cp, gamma.

parameters.name: Wall
parameters.description: MechanicalCondition NoSlip | Slip, ThermalCondition Isothermal | Adiabatic.

parameters.name: Sources
parameters.description: Normal Acceleration/Velocity/Displacement, Pressure, Lumped Port, Lumped Speaker Boundary, Monopole/Dipole Domain Source.

parameters.name: Impedance, Symmetry, Periodic Condition
parameters.description: Standard terminations.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module. Couples to structures through the Thermoviscous Acoustic SLNS-Structure Boundary coupling. For perforates or microperforated plates use full Thermoviscous Acoustics, Frequency Domain.

tools.name: Thermoviscous Acoustics Model (Thermoviscous Acoustics, Frequency Domain)
tools.description: Default domain node of the thermoviscous acoustics interfaces that defines the equilibrium pressure p0 and temperature T0 model inputs and the fluid properties entering the linearized Navier-Stokes, continuity and energy equations: dynamic and bulk viscosity, thermal conductivity, heat capacity, equilibrium density, coefficient of thermal expansion and isothermal compressibility. The extended thermal expansion and compressibility inputs allow any constitutive relation (ideal gas, liquids, tabulated data).
tools.usage: Thermoviscous Acoustics, Frequency Domain > Thermoviscous Acoustics Model 1 (tam1, default). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("ta").feature("tam1").set("BetaTOption", "FromSoundSpeed")

parameters.name: minput_pressure / minput_temperature
parameters.description: Equilibrium pressure p0 (default 1 atm) and temperature T0 (default 293.15 K).

parameters.name: mu, muB, kcond, Cp, rho0
parameters.description: Dynamic viscosity, bulk viscosity, thermal conductivity, heat capacity and equilibrium density (From material).

parameters.name: alpha_p
parameters.description: Coefficient of thermal expansion (from the equilibrium density or user defined).

parameters.name: BetaTOption, betaT, beta_s, c, gamma
parameters.description: Isothermal compressibility FromFluidDensity | FromSoundSpeed | FromIsentropicCompressibility | userdef.

parameters.name: gasConstantType, Rs, Mn
parameters.description: Ideal-gas constants when needed.

tools.notes: Evaluate ta.alpha0 and ta.betaT to make sure they are nonzero; wrong values are the most common source of errors. Boundary layer thicknesses ta.d_visc, ta.d_therm and the Prandtl number ta.Pr are available for mesh design.

tools.name: Wall (Thermoviscous Acoustics)
tools.description: Default boundary condition of the thermoviscous acoustics interfaces that combines a mechanical condition (No slip, the origin of the viscous boundary layer, or Slip) with a thermal condition (Isothermal, the origin of the thermal boundary layer, or Adiabatic). It covers most solid surfaces in microacoustic models; for moving walls use the Velocity condition or a structural multiphysics coupling, and for rarefied gas (Knudsen number 0.001-0.1) use Slip Wall.
tools.usage: Thermoviscous Acoustics > Wall 1 (wall1, default) or right-click > Wall. Java: model.component("comp1").physics("ta").create("wall2", "Wall", 2); feature("wall2").set("MechanicalCondition", "NoSlip")

parameters.name: MechanicalCondition
parameters.description: NoSlip (default) | Slip.

parameters.name: ThermalCondition
parameters.description: Isothermal (default) | Adiabatic.

tools.notes: With a PML, use no-slip at the outer PML boundary; Slip together with rational PML scaling causes a singularity. The Wall of the linearized Navier-Stokes interfaces has the same options.

tools.name: Slip Wall / Interior Slip Wall (Thermoviscous Acoustics)
tools.description: Nonideal wall conditions for the slip-flow regime (Knudsen number 0.001-0.1), relevant for MEMS microphones, micro-speakers and devices at low ambient pressure. The slip velocity depends linearly on the tangential wall stress, optionally with thermal creep, and a temperature jump is applied; coefficients follow the Maxwell model with accommodation coefficients, a slip length, or user values. The interior version models thin walls inside the fluid.
tools.usage: Right-click Thermoviscous Acoustics, Frequency Domain > Slip Wall (slw1) or Interior Conditions > Interior Slip Wall (islw1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("ta").create("slw1", "SlipWall", 2)

parameters.name: SlipCoefficients
parameters.description: Maxwell | UserDefined | SlipLength.

parameters.name: alpha_v, sigma_s, sigma_T, zeta_T, Ls
parameters.description: Tangential momentum accommodation, viscous/thermal slip coefficients, temperature jump coefficient, slip length.

parameters.name: MechanicalCondition, u_wall
parameters.description: FixedWall | MovingWall with wall velocity.

parameters.name: ThermalCondition, T_wall, NeglectThermalCreep
parameters.description: Isothermal | TemperatureVariation; option to neglect thermal creep.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module. The Lagrange-multiplier variables ta.slw1.lm_tau give the wall traction. Also used in viscous_damping_mpp.

tools.name: Port (Thermoviscous Acoustics, Frequency Domain)
tools.description: Waveguide port for thermoviscous acoustics that excites and absorbs a single propagating or evanescent mode including its nontrivial velocity and temperature boundary-layer profiles, which gives a far better termination of small ducts than an impedance or PML. Port types are plane wave (analytic lossy mode), slit, numeric (from a Thermoviscous Acoustics, Boundary Mode study) and user defined; S-parameters ta.S11, ta.S21, ... and, with two ports, the transfer matrix ta.T11..T22 are computed. A port sweep builds the full scattering matrix.
tools.usage: Right-click Thermoviscous Acoustics, Frequency Domain > Port (port1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("ta").create("port1", "Port", 2)

parameters.name: PortType
parameters.description: PlaneWave | Slit | Numeric | UserDefined.

parameters.name: PortExcitation, IncidentWave, pamp, P0, phi
parameters.description: Incident wave on/off defined by amplitude or power per unit length, and phase.

parameters.name: p, u, T, kn
parameters.description: User-defined mode shapes for pressure, velocity and temperature and the mode wave number.

parameters.name: PortArea, MultiplicationFactor, CircleRadius, a
parameters.description: Area/symmetry handling and circle radius for circular ducts.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module. Excite only one port at a time for S-parameters; do not apply one Port feature to several inlets. Also used in nonlinear_transfer_impedance, viscous_damping_mpp and wax_guard_acoustics.

tools.name: Lumped Speaker Boundary and Lumped Port (Thermoviscous Acoustics)
tools.description: Thermoviscous versions of the lumped transducer conditions: the Lumped Speaker Boundary (and Interior Lumped Speaker Boundary) couples a micro-speaker or receiver diaphragm, described by Thiele-Small parameters in an Electrical Circuit, to the thermoviscous field with a lumped back-volume model; the Lumped Port connects a small duct to a lumped circuit, a two-port transfer matrix or a lumped waveguide, assuming plane (0,0) modes. They allow electro-acoustic system models of hearing aids, earbuds and phone receivers without modeling the motor.
tools.usage: Right-click Thermoviscous Acoustics, Frequency Domain > Lumped Speaker Boundary (lsb1) / Lumped Port (lport1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("ta").create("lsb1", "LumpedSpeakerBoundary", 2); create("lport1", "LumpedPort", 2)

parameters.name: I_cir
parameters.description: Current from the circuit External I vs. U node.

parameters.name: BackVolumeAcousticImpedance, V_back, Rac, Lac, Cac, Zac
parameters.description: VolumeCompliance | RCL | UserDefined | NoCorrection back-volume model.

parameters.name: ThermalCondition, UseSlip
parameters.description: Isothermal | Adiabatic at the diaphragm and optional slip.

parameters.name: ConnectionType (Lumped Port)
parameters.description: Circuit | TwoPort | Waveguide, same options as the pressure acoustics Lumped Port.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module. The transient interface (tatd) also has Lumped Speaker Boundary and Interior Lumped Speaker Boundary; SLNS has Lumped Port and Lumped Speaker Boundary.

tools.name: Background Acoustic Fields (Thermoviscous Acoustics, Frequency Domain)
tools.description: Domain feature that defines background acoustic pressure, velocity and temperature variation (pb, ub, Tb) so that the interface solves for the scattered field; used for scattering problems such as a small particle or bubble in a sound field or acoustophoresis. The field can be a user-defined expression (e.g. from a previous pressure-acoustics study) or a lossy plane wave defined by amplitude and direction, with material data from the model.
tools.usage: Right-click Thermoviscous Acoustics, Frequency Domain > Background Acoustic Fields (baf1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("ta").create("baf1", "BackgroundAcousticFields", 3)

parameters.name: AcousticFieldType
parameters.description: UserDefined (default) | PlaneWave.

parameters.name: p, u, T
parameters.description: Background acoustic pressure, velocity and temperature variation (user defined).

parameters.name: pamp, e_k
parameters.description: Pressure amplitude and wave direction for the plane wave.

parameters.name: FluidMaterial
parameters.description: Material data source for the plane-wave option.

tools.notes: For waveguide inlets prefer the Port condition. Total fields ta.p_t, ta.T_t are used in postprocessing. LNS and LE interfaces have their own Background Acoustic Fields nodes.

tools.name: Nonlinear Thermoviscous Acoustics Contributions (Thermoviscous Acoustics, Transient)
tools.description: Adds all second-order nonlinear terms of the acoustic perturbation fields to the transient thermoviscous equations, including the nonlinear convective terms needed for vortex shedding and flow detachment at perforates, grills and miniature sound ports, and optionally a second-order density expansion for high-SPL equation-of-state nonlinearity. It is required when the particle velocity is no longer small compared with the speed of sound, producing harmonic distortion and nonlinear (amplitude-dependent) transfer impedance.
tools.usage: Right-click Thermoviscous Acoustics, Transient > Nonlinear Thermoviscous Acoustics Contributions (ntac1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("tatd").create("ntac1", "NonlinearThermoviscousAcousticsContributions", 2)

parameters.name: DensityExpansion
parameters.description: FirstOrder | SecondOrder equation of state.

parameters.name: MaterialDataOption, BA, beta, gamma
parameters.description: Nonlinearity data as B/A, coefficient of nonlinearity or ratio of specific heats.

parameters.name: d2rhodp2, d2rhodpdT, d2rhodT2 (+ _option)
parameters.description: Second-order density derivatives, from the equilibrium density or user defined.

parameters.name: IncludeViscousDissipation
parameters.description: Include viscous dissipation in the energy equation.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module. Resolve harmonics in mesh and time step; consider a coarser pressure-acoustics region coupled via Acoustic-Thermoviscous Acoustic Boundary. Also used in thermoacoustic_engine_heat_pump.

tools.name: Interior Wall / Interior Velocity / Interior Temperature Variation (Thermoviscous Acoustics)
tools.description: Interior (slit) conditions of the thermoviscous interfaces that avoid meshing thin structures. Interior Wall applies no-slip or slip and isothermal or adiabatic conditions on both sides of an interior boundary with discontinuous fields; Interior Velocity prescribes velocity components on an interior boundary (e.g. a diaphragm driven by a lumped model) with an option for continuous pressure; Interior Temperature Variation imposes a harmonic temperature Tbnd on a thin sheet, for thermophones or ohmically heated films.
tools.usage: Right-click Thermoviscous Acoustics > Interior Conditions > Interior Wall (iwall1) / Interior Velocity (ivel1) / Interior Temperature Variation (itv1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("ta").create("iwall1", "InteriorWall", 2); create("ivel1", "InteriorVelocity", 2); create("itv1", "InteriorTemperatureVariation", 2)

parameters.name: MechanicalCondition / ThermalCondition
parameters.description: No slip or Slip (perfect); Isothermal or Adiabatic.

parameters.name: u0, Direction, coordinateSystem, ContinuousPressure
parameters.description: Prescribed velocity components (Interior Velocity) and pressure continuity option.

parameters.name: Tbnd
parameters.description: Temperature variation for Interior Temperature Variation (K).

tools.notes: Interior Impedance (ta) adds a transfer impedance between the two sides. Use up()/down() operators to evaluate one-sided values.

tools.name: Surface Tension (Thermoviscous Acoustics, Frequency Domain)
tools.description: Interior condition modeling an interface between two immiscible fluids with surface tension, using a linearized (acoustic perturbation) Young-Laplace equation around the static curved interface: the normal stress jumps by the surface tension times the perturbed curvature while velocity and temperature variation are continuous. Important for microbubbles and microdroplets, e.g. bubble eigenmodes and ultrasound contrast agents.
tools.usage: Right-click Thermoviscous Acoustics, Frequency Domain > Interior Conditions > Surface Tension (sten1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("ta").create("sten1", "SurfaceTension", 1)

parameters.name: SurfaceTensionCoefficient
parameters.description: LibraryCoefficientLiquidGas | LibraryCoefficientLiquidLiquid | LibraryCoefficientLiquidMixtureGas | userdef.

parameters.name: LibraryCoefficientLiquidGas (e.g. WaterAir)
parameters.description: Built-in library pairs; liquid/liquid and predefined mixtures with mass fraction inputs.

parameters.name: sigma
parameters.description: User-defined surface tension coefficient (N/m).

tools.notes: The normal acoustic displacement of the interface is available as ta.sten1.dn.

tools.name: Mechanical and Thermal Conditions (Thermoviscous Acoustics)
tools.description: Individual boundary conditions of the thermoviscous interfaces that can be combined instead of the default Wall: mechanical No Slip, Slip (perfect), Velocity (prescribed u0, e.g. a vibrating source), No Stress and Boundary Stress (stress tensor, traction or pressure), and thermal Isothermal, Adiabatic, Temperature Variation (Tbnd) and Heat Flux. Pressure (Adiabatic) prescribes a pressure with zero heat flux, and Symmetry and Periodic Condition complete the set.
tools.usage: Right-click Thermoviscous Acoustics > Mechanical Conditions / Thermal Conditions submenus. Java: model.component("comp1").physics("ta").create("velt1", "VelocityThermoacoustic", 2); create("noslip1", "NoSlip", 2); create("iso1", "Isothermal", 2); create("temp1", "TemperatureVariation", 2); create("hfl1", "HeatFlux", 2); create("str1", "BoundaryStress", 2); create("pra1", "PressureAdiabatic", 2)

parameters.name: u0 (Velocity)
parameters.description: Prescribed velocity components with per-direction checkboxes and coordinate system.

parameters.name: Stress type (Boundary Stress)
parameters.description: Stress tensor | Traction (default) | Pressure.

parameters.name: Tbnd (Temperature Variation)
parameters.description: Harmonic temperature variation amplitude.

parameters.name: pbnd (Pressure (Adiabatic))
parameters.description: Prescribed pressure.

tools.notes: A mechanical and a thermal condition must both be defined on each exterior boundary. Couple temperature to a solid heat-transfer model with the Thermoviscous Acoustic-Thermal Perturbation Boundary.

tools.name: Linearized Euler, Frequency Domain (lef)
tools.description: Frequency-domain aeroacoustics interface solving the linearized continuity, momentum (Euler) and energy equations for acoustic density, velocity and pressure on top of a stationary ideal-gas background mean flow that may be rotational and nonuniform. Suited for jet noise propagation, flow ducts and nozzles where refraction and convection by the mean flow matter but viscous and thermal losses do not; the full formulation or the linearized perturbed compressible equations (LPCE) can be chosen. Uses GLS stabilization and supports PMLs and Asymptotic Far-Field Radiation.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Acoustics > Aeroacoustics > Linearized Euler, Frequency Domain; background flow via model inputs or Background Fluid Flow Coupling; Study > Frequency Domain. Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("lef", "LinearizedEulerFrequency", "geom1")

parameters.name: Linearized Euler Model (lem1)
parameters.description: Background mean flow rho0, u0, p0 and ideal-gas properties gamma, Cp, Rs; gradient term suppression.

parameters.name: Linearized Euler Equation Settings
parameters.description: Full linearized Euler or LPCE formulation.

parameters.name: Stabilization
parameters.description: GLS (recommended), SUPG, none or legacy.

parameters.name: Boundary nodes
parameters.description: Rigid Wall, Moving Wall, Impedance, Asymptotic Far-Field Radiation with Outflow Boundary, Prescribed Acoustic Fields, Pressure (Isentropic).

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module. Nonacoustic vorticity/entropy waves are supported and can grow (e.g. Kelvin-Helmholtz instabilities); use gradient-term suppression if needed. For Ma < 0.1 plain Pressure Acoustics with space-dependent c and rho is usually enough.

tools.name: Linearized Euler, Transient (let)
tools.description: Time-domain linearized Euler interface for acoustic density, velocity and pressure perturbations in a stationary ideal-gas mean flow, with a scattered-field formulation and Background Acoustic Fields. Because the equations are lossless, nonacoustic modes and instabilities can grow in time; open boundaries are handled with absorbing layers. Typical uses are pulse propagation through jets and time-of-flight studies with flow.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Acoustics > Aeroacoustics > Linearized Euler, Transient; Study > Time Dependent. Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("let", "LinearizedEulerTransient", "geom1")

parameters.name: Linearized Euler Model
parameters.description: Background flow and ideal-gas data, gradient term suppression (GTSrho0, GTSu0, GTSp0, GTSconv).

parameters.name: Domain Sources
parameters.description: Mass, momentum (acceleration or volume force) and energy (pressure rate or heat) sources.

parameters.name: Absorbing Layer (Definitions)
parameters.description: Sponge layers for open boundaries.

parameters.name: Specific Acoustic Impedance (Isentropic)
parameters.description: Simple nonreflecting condition at the outer boundary of absorbing layers.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module. See 'Absorbing Layers for the Linearized Euler, Transient Interface' in the modeling section.

tools.name: Linearized Euler, Boundary Mode (lebm)
tools.description: Boundary mode analysis of ducts with a stationary ideal-gas mean flow that is uniform in the propagation direction, solving for the acoustic density, velocity and pressure mode shapes and out-of-plane wave numbers on an inlet or cross section. Used to set up modal sources in waveguides with flow, e.g. engine inlets and exhaust ducts. Available in 3D and 2D axisymmetry on boundaries.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Acoustics > Aeroacoustics > Linearized Euler, Boundary Mode; Study > Mode Analysis. Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("lebm", "LinearizedEulerBoundaryMode", "geom1")

parameters.name: Linearized Euler Model
parameters.description: Background flow and gas properties on the boundary.

parameters.name: Rigid Wall, Impedance, Specific Acoustic Impedance (Isentropic)
parameters.description: Edge conditions around the cross section.

parameters.name: Mode Analysis: modeFreq, neigs, shift
parameters.description: Frequency and number of modes.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module. Default nodes: Linearized Euler Model, Rigid Wall, Initial Values (plus Axial Symmetry in 2D axi).

tools.name: Linearized Navier-Stokes, Transient (lnst)
tools.description: Time-domain linearized Navier-Stokes interface for acoustic pressure, velocity and temperature in any stationary isothermal or nonisothermal background flow, including viscous and thermal losses and viscous-dissipation heating. It is the transient version of lnsf and is used for time-domain flow-acoustic interaction, e.g. transient response of liners or flow sensors; flow-induced noise itself is not included.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Acoustics > Aeroacoustics > Linearized Navier-Stokes, Transient; Study > Time Dependent. Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("lnst", "LinearizedNavierStokesTransient", "geom1")

parameters.name: Linearized Navier-Stokes Model
parameters.description: Background flow (u0, p0, T0), fluid properties, stabilization.

parameters.name: Wall, No Slip, Slip, Isothermal, Adiabatic
parameters.description: Mechanical and thermal conditions.

parameters.name: Impedance (lnst)
parameters.description: Time-domain impedance including RCL models.

parameters.name: Domain Sources
parameters.description: Mass, volume force and heat sources.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module. With u0 = 0 the equations reduce to thermoviscous acoustics (which uses P1-P2-P2 and no stabilization by default).

tools.name: Linearized Navier-Stokes, Boundary Mode (lnsbm)
tools.description: Boundary mode analysis in ducts with any stationary isothermal or nonisothermal mean flow uniform in the propagation direction, including all viscous and thermal losses (acoustic boundary layers) and flow interaction. It returns mode shapes of pressure, velocity and temperature and complex axial wave numbers, e.g. to define lossy modal sources for liner studies in nacelles.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Acoustics > Aeroacoustics > Linearized Navier-Stokes, Boundary Mode; Study > Mode Analysis. Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("lnsbm", "LinearizedNavierStokesBoundaryMode", "geom1")

parameters.name: Linearized Navier-Stokes Model (lnsm1)
parameters.description: Background flow and fluid properties.

parameters.name: Wall (MechanicalCondition, ThermalCondition)
parameters.description: Edge conditions.

parameters.name: Impedance (lnsbm)
parameters.description: Liner impedance on the duct wall edges.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module.

tools.name: Linearized Potential Flow, Frequency Domain (lpff)
tools.description: Solves for the acoustic velocity potential in an inviscid, irrotational (potential) background mean flow with Ma < 1, typically computed with the Compressible Potential Flow interface. It is the most efficient convected-acoustics model for turbofan inlets, nacelle liners and flow ducts, with Ingard-Myers/Brambley liner impedances, modal Ports (circular/annular spinning modes), Vortex Sheets for jet shear layers and mass-flow sources. Pressure is derived from the potential (lpff.p, lpff.Lp).
tools.usage: Add Physics > Acoustics > Aeroacoustics > Linearized Potential Flow, Frequency Domain; couple the mean flow with Background Potential Flow Coupling; Study > Frequency Domain. Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("lpff", "LinearizedPotentialFlowFrequency", "geom1")

parameters.name: Linearized Potential Flow Model (lpfm1)
parameters.description: Background velocity (model input), density rho0 and speed of sound c0.

parameters.name: Port
parameters.description: Modal inlet/outlet conditions with S-parameters.

parameters.name: Impedance, Interior Impedance
parameters.description: Liner impedances with Ingard-Myers or Brambley flow boundary conditions.

parameters.name: Vortex Sheet, Plane Wave Radiation, Incident Velocity Potential
parameters.description: Shear layers and open boundaries.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module. Supersedes the older aepf tag referenced in some catalog entries. Mode Analysis is available in 2D and 1D axisymmetry. Also used in generic_nacelle_liner, jet_pipe and sound_radiation_circular_duct.

tools.name: Linearized Potential Flow, Transient (lpft)
tools.description: Time-domain version of the linearized potential flow interface: solves for the acoustic velocity potential in a subsonic potential mean flow for transient signals, e.g. pulse propagation through a flow duct or Doppler-shifted moving sources. Features include normal mass flow, velocity potential, plane wave radiation, mass-flow point/edge/circular sources and symmetry.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Acoustics > Aeroacoustics > Linearized Potential Flow, Transient; Study > Time Dependent. Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("lpft", "LinearizedPotentialFlowTransient", "geom1")

parameters.name: Linearized Potential Flow Model
parameters.description: Background flow (from Compressible Potential Flow) and fluid properties.

parameters.name: Mass Flow Point/Edge/Circular Source
parameters.description: Transient sources.

parameters.name: Plane Wave Radiation
parameters.description: Open boundaries.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module. Limited to Ma < 1.

tools.name: Linearized Potential Flow, Boundary Mode (lpfbm)
tools.description: Solves the eigenvalue problem for convected duct modes on a boundary in the presence of a compressible potential mean flow, returning out-of-plane wave numbers and mode shapes at a given frequency. Used to compute the numeric modes for Port conditions of Linearized Potential Flow, Frequency Domain, including modes of lined ducts with impedance edges.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Acoustics > Aeroacoustics > Linearized Potential Flow, Boundary Mode; Study > Mode Analysis. Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("lpfbm", "LinearizedPotentialFlowBoundaryMode", "geom1")

parameters.name: Linearized Potential Flow Model
parameters.description: Background flow on the boundary (propagation direction, ReverseNormal).

parameters.name: Impedance (lpfbm)
parameters.description: Lined edges (Ingard-Myers or Brambley with boundary layer thickness delta).

parameters.name: Mode Analysis settings
parameters.description: modeFreq, neigs, shift.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module. Solutions are referenced by a numeric Port in lpff (phi_i/phi_o and kn_i/kn_o).

tools.name: Compressible Potential Flow (cpf)
tools.description: Computes a subsonic, inviscid, irrotational, isentropic compressible mean flow by solving for the velocity potential and density; pressure, velocity and (optionally) temperature are derived. It provides the background mean flow for the Linearized Potential Flow interfaces, e.g. the flow in a turbofan inlet or a flow duct, and supports one unique inlet since a global total energy definition is used.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Acoustics > Aeroacoustics > Compressible Potential Flow; Study > Stationary; then couple with Background Potential Flow Coupling. Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("cpf", "CompressiblePotentialFlow", "geom1")

parameters.name: Compressible Potential Flow Model (cpf1)
parameters.description: Ratio of specific heats gamma (default 1.4), force potential, CalculateTemperature with Rs.

parameters.name: Mass Flow (mf1): rho_bnd, vn
parameters.description: Inlet mass flow condition defined by boundary density and normal velocity.

parameters.name: Normal Flow, Slip Velocity, Mean Flow Velocity Potential
parameters.description: Outlet, wall (default) and prescribed-potential conditions.

parameters.name: Initial Values: Phi, rho
parameters.description: Initial potential and density (good guesses help convergence).

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module. Not valid for flows with vorticity, strong shear layers or shocks; use CFD with Linearized Euler/Navier-Stokes instead.

tools.name: Imported Fluid Flow (iff)
tools.description: Maps CFD results stored in CGNS files (via the CFD Data (CGNS) function under Global Definitions) consistently onto the COMSOL mesh so that external flow data can drive aeroacoustic models as if computed by a COMSOL Fluid Flow interface. It feeds the Background Fluid Flow Coupling (with the Mapping study) or the Aeroacoustic Flow Source Coupling (with Transient Mapping), or simply provides pressure loads for vibroacoustics. Pressure, density, velocity components, temperature and turbulent viscosity can be mapped on domains or boundaries.
tools.usage: Global Definitions > Functions > CFD Data (CGNS); Add Physics > Acoustics > Aeroacoustics > Imported Fluid Flow; Study > Mapping. Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("iff", "ImportedFluidFlow", "geom1"); model.func().create("cgns1", "CGNS")

parameters.name: Flow Import (fi1): ImportedData
parameters.description: The CFD Data (CGNS) function to map from.

parameters.name: p, rho, u (u1,u2,u3), T, mu_eff
parameters.description: Function names per mapped field; unmapped velocity components are set to zero.

parameters.name: smoothingMethod, delta_diff, useDensityConstraint
parameters.description: Smoothing and constraint options for the mapped fields.

parameters.name: No Slip, Symmetry
parameters.description: Boundary conditions applied to the mapped velocity.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module or the CFD Module; the CGNS function is Windows-only. The CGNS function tag/type ('CGNS') was read from the helmholtz_resonator_with_flow_cgns model (FunctionFeature op CGNS).

tools.name: Linearized Euler Model (Linearized Euler)
tools.description: Domain node of the linearized Euler interfaces that sets up the governing equations (full formulation or LPCE), defines the background mean flow (density, velocity, pressure as model inputs, often from a CFD solution) and the ideal-gas properties, and offers gradient term suppression (GTS) as an advanced stabilization of the mean-flow gradient terms that can drive instabilities. Source terms are added with Domain Sources.
tools.usage: Linearized Euler, Frequency Domain/Transient/Boundary Mode > Linearized Euler Model 1 (lem1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("lef").feature("lem1").set("GTSconv", "1")

parameters.name: rho0, minput_velocity, minput_pressure
parameters.description: Background mean flow density, velocity and pressure (user defined or from a flow interface).

parameters.name: gamma, Cp, cporgamma, Rs, Mn, gasconsttype
parameters.description: Ideal-gas properties.

parameters.name: GTSrho0, GTSu0, GTSp0, GTSconv
parameters.description: Suppress mean-flow density/velocity/pressure gradient terms or all convective terms (Advanced Physics Options).

tools.notes: The background flow must be stationary; when taken from CFD use the Background Fluid Flow Coupling and a Mapping study for consistent mesh-to-mesh transfer.

tools.name: Linearized Navier-Stokes Model (Linearized Navier-Stokes)
tools.description: Domain node of the linearized Navier-Stokes interfaces that sets up the linearized continuity, momentum and energy equations with viscous stress, heat conduction and viscous dissipation, defines the background mean flow (velocity, pressure, temperature) and the fluid constitutive data (compressibility and thermal expansion from density, sound speed or isentropic compressibility). The effective viscosity including eddy viscosity from a turbulent CFD solution (spf.mu_eff) can be used through the Background Fluid Flow Coupling to model turbulent attenuation.
tools.usage: Linearized Navier-Stokes, Frequency Domain > Linearized Navier-Stokes Model 1 (lnsm1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("lnsf").feature("lnsm1").set("BetaTOption", "FromSoundSpeed")

parameters.name: minput_velocity, minput_pressure, minput_temperature, rho0
parameters.description: Background mean flow fields (from a flow interface or user defined).

parameters.name: mu, muB, kcond, Cp, gamma, c0
parameters.description: Fluid transport and thermodynamic properties.

parameters.name: BetaTOption, betaT, alpha_p, beta_s
parameters.description: Isothermal compressibility and thermal expansion definitions.

parameters.name: bolViscDiss, GTSu0, GTSp0, GTST0, GTSrho0, GTSconv
parameters.description: Viscous dissipation and gradient term suppression options.

tools.notes: Plot lnsf.CellPe_v and lnsf.CellPe_th to check the cell Peclet number; GLS stabilization is recommended. Turbulent viscosity from RANS can overestimate attenuation; SST gives better estimates.

tools.name: First-Order Material Parameters (Linearized Navier-Stokes)
tools.description: Advanced domain subnode that includes the acoustic (first-order) variation of material parameters about their background values, i.e. derivatives of viscosity, bulk viscosity, heat capacity, thermal conductivity and thermal expansion with respect to pressure and temperature, optionally correcting the viscous dissipation function. It matters in strongly nonisothermal flows, such as thermoacoustic devices or hot exhaust ducts.
tools.usage: Show More Options > Advanced Physics Options; right-click Linearized Navier-Stokes > First-Order Material Parameters (fompd1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("lnsf").create("fompd1", "FirstOrderMaterialParam", 3)

parameters.name: bolViscAco, bolBulkViscAco
parameters.description: Include derivatives of dynamic and bulk viscosity.

parameters.name: bolCpAco, bolkcondAco, bolalpha0Aco
parameters.description: Include derivatives of heat capacity, thermal conductivity and thermal expansion coefficient.

parameters.name: bolCorrViscDiss
parameters.description: Include the correction to the viscous dissipation function.

tools.notes: Available in the frequency-domain, transient and boundary-mode LNS interfaces.

tools.name: Asymptotic Far-Field Radiation / Outflow Boundary (Linearized Euler)
tools.description: Nonreflecting open boundary of the linearized Euler interfaces based on the asymptotic far-field behavior of spherical (3D/axi) or cylindrical (2D) waves from a compact source, the Tam and Dong condition, applied to the scattered field. A default Outflow Boundary subnode must be placed where the mean flow leaves the domain so that vorticity and entropy waves exit without reflection; it must not be used where there is no flow (u0 = 0) or at inflow boundaries.
tools.usage: Right-click Linearized Euler > Asymptotic Far-Field Radiation (affr1); Outflow Boundary (ob1) subnode. Java: model.component("comp1").physics("lef").create("affr1", "AsymptoticFarFieldRadiation", 1); feature("affr1").create("ob1", "OutflowBoundary", 1)

parameters.name: Source location r0
parameters.description: Center of the compact source used in the asymptotic condition.

parameters.name: Outflow Boundary selection
parameters.description: Boundaries where the mean flow exits.

tools.notes: The condition assumes k*r >> 1; place it far from the source or use PMLs. The subnode tag 'ob' and type OutflowBoundary come from the completion data (topic lef_ob).

tools.name: Moving Wall (Linearized Euler)
tools.description: Wall condition for a harmonically vibrating surface in the presence of a mean flow, formulated as a variant of the Ingard-Myers condition so that the grazing flow over the moving wall is accounted for. The motion is given as inward normal displacement (default), displacement field, inward normal velocity or velocity field; used for vibrating panels or pistons in flow ducts.
tools.usage: Right-click Linearized Euler > Wall Conditions > Moving Wall (movw1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("lef").create("movw1", "MovingWall", 2)

parameters.name: selNormDisp
parameters.description: inwardNormalDisplacement | displacementField | invardNormalVelocity | velocityField (tokens as in the completion data).

parameters.name: vn_w, v_w, un_w, u_w
parameters.description: Inward normal displacement, displacement field, inward normal velocity or velocity field.

tools.notes: Rigid Wall is the default stationary wall. For two-way coupling with a structure use the Aeroacoustic-Structure Boundary coupling.

tools.name: Domain Sources (Linearized Euler / Linearized Navier-Stokes)
tools.description: Volumetric source terms on the right-hand side of the linearized continuity, momentum and energy equations of the aeroacoustic interfaces, used to represent compact acoustic sources (e.g. a point-like monopole in a jet), heat-release sources or user-defined analogy source terms. In linearized Euler the momentum source is an acceleration or a volume force and the energy source a pressure rate of change or heat source; in linearized Navier-Stokes they are mass, volume force and heat sources.
tools.usage: Right-click Linearized Euler (or Linearized Navier-Stokes) > Domain Sources (leds1 / lnsds1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("lef").create("leds1", "DomainSources", 2)

parameters.name: M (LE) / S_continuity (LNS)
parameters.description: Mass source.

parameters.name: MomentumSourceType, A, F (LE) / S_momentum (LNS)
parameters.description: Acceleration or volume force source.

parameters.name: EnergySourceType, p_rc, Q (LE) / S_energy (LNS)
parameters.description: Pressure rate of change or heat source.

tools.notes: The coupling to the mean flow does not generate flow-induced noise by itself; for flow-noise sources use the Aeroacoustic Flow Source in pressure acoustics.

tools.name: Impedance (Linearized Potential Flow)
tools.description: Liner impedance condition for convected acoustics in a potential mean flow, defining Zn = p/(n.v) for acoustic liners in turbofan nacelles and flow ducts. Two flow formulations exist: Ingard-Myers, which assumes an infinitely thin hydrodynamic boundary layer, and Brambley, which includes refraction in a finite linear boundary layer of thickness delta and is better behaved numerically.
tools.usage: Right-click Linearized Potential Flow, Frequency Domain (or Boundary Mode) > Impedance (imp1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("lpff").create("imp1", "Impedance", 2)

parameters.name: ImpedanceModel
parameters.description: IngardMyers (default) | Brambley.

parameters.name: Zn
parameters.description: Specific impedance (Pa*s/m), typically frequency dependent.

parameters.name: delta
parameters.description: Turbulent boundary layer thickness of the background mean flow (Brambley).

tools.notes: Linearized Euler and Navier-Stokes have their own Impedance nodes (lef: grazing flow option bolWallImp; lnsf: RCL models and tangential velocity No slip/Slip).

tools.name: Vortex Sheet (Linearized Potential Flow)
tools.description: Interior (or pair) boundary condition that represents a thin shear layer separating a flowing stream from the surrounding fluid, such as the edge of a jet exhausting from a pipe or engine. The velocity potential is discontinuous across the sheet: normal stress (pressure) and normal displacement are continuous while the tangential velocity may jump; an extra degree of freedom lpff.vs1.w (normal displacement of the sheet) is solved for.
tools.usage: Right-click Linearized Potential Flow, Frequency Domain > Interior Conditions > Vortex Sheet (vs1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("lpff").create("vs1", "VortexSheet", 1)

parameters.name: Boundary selection
parameters.description: Interior boundary along the shear layer, starting at the trailing edge of the duct lip.

tools.notes: Only applicable on interior boundaries or pairs; the vortex sheet position must be defined geometrically.

tools.name: Port (Linearized Potential Flow, Frequency Domain)
tools.description: Modal port for convected acoustics in a potential mean flow: excites and absorbs one propagating duct mode per port feature and provides S-parameters, used for turbofan modal source decomposition and lined-duct transmission. Port types are Circular and Annular (standardized spinning modes with azimuthal and radial order) or User defined (incident and outgoing mode shapes and wave numbers from a boundary mode study); incident power, pressure amplitude, potential amplitude or mode scale can define the excitation.
tools.usage: Right-click Linearized Potential Flow, Frequency Domain > Port (port1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("lpff").create("port1", "Port", 2)

parameters.name: PortType
parameters.description: Circular | Annular | UserDefined.

parameters.name: m_circ, n_circ, AzimuthalDependency
parameters.description: Azimuthal and radial mode numbers and sine/cosine dependency.

parameters.name: IncidentWave, P0, pamp, phiamp, Sin, phi
parameters.description: Power | PressureAmplitude | VelocityPotentialAmplitude | ModeScale excitation.

parameters.name: phi_i, kn_i, phi_o, kn_o, OutgoingMode
parameters.description: User-defined incident/outgoing mode shapes and wave numbers.

parameters.name: UniformNormalFlow, u0n
parameters.description: Uniform outward normal mean flow at the port (average or user defined).

tools.notes: Include ports for all cut-on modes in the frequency range to obtain a fully nonreflecting termination; Port Reference Axis sets the azimuthal orientation.

tools.name: Mass Flow Sources (Linearized Potential Flow)
tools.description: Point, edge and circular sources of the linearized potential flow interfaces that inject a harmonic (or transient) mass flow into a moving medium, e.g. a monopole convected by a jet or a Doppler-shifted moving source. Mass Flow Point Source is used in 2D/3D, Mass Flow Edge Source on edges in 3D, Mass Flow Circular Source off-axis in 2D axisymmetry and Mass Flow Line Source on Axis on the symmetry axis; Normal Mass Flow prescribes an inward mass flow on boundaries.
tools.usage: Right-click Linearized Potential Flow > Points / Edges > Mass Flow ... Source. Java: model.component("comp1").physics("lpff").create("mfps1", "MassFlowPointSource", 0)  (also "MassFlowEdgeSource", "MassFlowCircularSource", "MassFlowAxiSource"; boundary "NormalMassFlow" with property mn)

parameters.name: Mass flow amplitude
parameters.description: Point/line mass flow rate of the source.

parameters.name: mn (Normal Mass Flow)
parameters.description: Inward mass flow per unit area on a boundary.

tools.notes: Property names of the point/edge source amplitude are not listed in the local completion data; set them in the GUI and read back with properties().

tools.name: Convected Wave Equation Model (Convected Wave Equation, Time Explicit)
tools.description: Domain node of the Convected Wave Equation, Time Explicit (cwe) interface that solves the linearized Euler (adiabatic, moving-medium acoustics) equations with the dG time-explicit method for large ultrasound problems in a stationary background flow, such as time-of-flight flowmeters. Background density, velocity, pressure and speed of sound are model inputs that may vary smoothly in space; losses use the general dissipation model, and a filter can suppress physical instabilities (vorticity waves).
tools.usage: Convected Wave Equation, Time Explicit > Convected Wave Equation Model 1 (cwem1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("cwe", "ConvectedWaveEquation", "geom1"); physics("cwe").feature("cwem1").set("FluidModel", "GeneralDissipation")

parameters.name: minput_velocity, minput_pressure, rho0, c0
parameters.description: Background mean flow velocity, pressure, density and speed of sound (e.g. from a CFD solution).

parameters.name: FluidModel, delta_diff
parameters.description: LinearElastic | GeneralDissipation with sound diffusivity.

parameters.name: LFtau
parameters.description: Lax-Friedrichs flux parameter.

parameters.name: ActivateFilter
parameters.description: Enable filtering to stabilize physical instabilities.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module. Map CFD data with the Mapping study for consistency; add Absorbing Layers plus Specific Acoustic Impedance (Isentropic) (type AcousticImpedance, property Zn) at the outer boundaries. Without a coupling, enter the background velocity directly in minput_velocity (user defined).

tools.name: Nonlinear Pressure Acoustics, Time Explicit (nate)
tools.description: dG time-explicit interface for nonlinear finite-amplitude acoustic waves in domains spanning many wavelengths, solving the nonlinear continuity and momentum equations (no superposition, so total fields equal the dependent variables). Applications include HIFU, ultrasonic imaging with harmonic generation, shock formation in sirens and nonlinear cylindrical/spherical waves. Features include lossy fluid models, sources, impedance with first/second-order pressure-velocity relation, material discontinuity and min/max pressure tracking; adaptive mesh refinement and shock-capturing are discussed for highly nonlinear problems.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Acoustics > Ultrasound > Nonlinear Pressure Acoustics, Time Explicit; Study > Time Dependent. Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("nate", "NonlinearPressureAcousticsTimeExplicit", "geom1")

parameters.name: Nonlinear Pressure Acoustics, Time Explicit Model (natem1)
parameters.description: Fluid model and nonlinearity (B/A or beta).

parameters.name: Pressure, Normal Velocity, Mass/Volume Force/Heat Source
parameters.description: Excitation of the transducer surface or domain.

parameters.name: Impedance: PressureVelocityRelation
parameters.description: FirstOrder | SecondOrder relation for the nonreflecting impedance.

parameters.name: Absorbing Layer (Definitions)
parameters.description: Sponge layers for open boundaries.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module. For linear problems with scattered fields use Pressure Acoustics, Time Explicit. Also used in nonlinear_cylindrical_wave.

tools.name: Nonlinear Pressure Acoustics, Time Explicit Model (Nonlinear Pressure Acoustics, Time Explicit)
tools.description: Default domain node of the nate interface defining the fluid model (linear elastic, viscous, thermally conducting, thermoviscous, general dissipation, ideal gas), model inputs and the coefficient of nonlinearity (from the parameter of nonlinearity B/A or user defined) for the nonlinear continuity and momentum equations. It also holds the dG flux parameter and filter; space-dependent material data from interpolation functions can be accelerated by using spatial coordinates as arguments.
tools.usage: Nonlinear Pressure Acoustics, Time Explicit > Nonlinear Pressure Acoustics, Time Explicit Model 1 (natem1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("nate").feature("natem1").set("CoefficientOfNonlinearity", "FromParamOfNonlin")

parameters.name: FluidModel
parameters.description: LinearElastic | Viscous | Thermal | Viscothermal | GeneralDissipation | IdealGas.

parameters.name: CoefficientOfNonlinearity, BA, beta
parameters.description: FromParamOfNonlin (B/A) | UserDefined (beta).

parameters.name: c, rho, delta_diff
parameters.description: Speed of sound, density and sound diffusivity.

parameters.name: LFtau, ActivateFilter
parameters.description: Lax-Friedrichs flux parameter and filter.

tools.notes: Use enough elements per wavelength of the highest harmonic to be resolved; see 'Solving Highly Nonlinear Problems' and 'Adaptive Mesh Refinement' in the user's guide.

tools.name: Compute Minimum and Maximum Pressure (Nonlinear Pressure Acoustics, Time Explicit)
tools.description: Subfeature of the Nonlinear Pressure Acoustics, Time Explicit Model, applicable on domains or boundaries, that tracks the minimum and maximum pressure over time at every point and stores them as nate.p_min and nate.p_max. These are used to visualize focal zones, peak rarefactional and compressional pressure (e.g. for mechanical index) in HIFU and therapeutic ultrasound without storing every time step.
tools.usage: Right-click Nonlinear Pressure Acoustics, Time Explicit Model > Compute Minimum and Maximum Pressure (mmp1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("nate").feature("natem1").create("mmp1", "MinMaxPressure", 2)

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Domains or boundaries where min/max are tracked.

tools.notes: The feature solves extra variables; restrict the selection to the region of interest.

tools.name: Absorbing Layer (time-explicit acoustics and elastic waves)
tools.description: Definitions node that turns outer domains into sponge layers for the dG time-explicit interfaces (Convected Wave Equation, Pressure Acoustics, Nonlinear Pressure Acoustics and Elastic Waves, Time Explicit, and Linearized Euler, Transient). It combines a coordinate scaling that slows waves and aligns them normal to the outer boundary, filtering of high-frequency content controlled at the physics level, and a simple nonreflecting condition at the layer's outer boundary, reducing reflections by a factor of 100-1000.
tools.usage: Definitions > Absorbing Layer (ab1) on the layer domains; add Specific Acoustic Impedance (Isentropic) or Low-Reflecting Boundary on the outer boundary. Java: model.component("comp1").coordSystem().create("ab1", "AbsorbingLayer"); coordSystem("ab1").selection().named("layers")

parameters.name: ScalingType
parameters.description: Cartesian | cylindrical | spherical | userDefined geometry type.

parameters.name: width
parameters.description: Physical width of the layer.

parameters.name: pole
parameters.description: Pole distance of the scaling.

parameters.name: Filter Parameters for Absorbing Layers (physics level)
parameters.description: Filter strength; should not be too aggressive.

tools.notes: The layer should hold 2-3 mesh elements (about one largest wavelength) and avoid small elements, which reduce the explicit time step. Inspect the scaled coordinates x_absorb_ab1 etc. Also used in porous_absorber_time_domain, ground_motion_seismic_event and angle_beam_ndt.

tools.name: Elastic Waves, Time Explicit Model (Elastic Waves, Time Explicit)
tools.description: Default domain node of the Elastic Waves, Time Explicit (elte) interface that solves the velocity-strain formulation of linear elastodynamics with the dG method and explicit time stepping, for isotropic, orthotropic or fully anisotropic materials. It targets wave propagation over many wavelengths: ultrasonic NDT (angle beam, Lamb waves), seismic waves and wave propagation in anisotropic samples; P and S wave speeds elte.cp and elte.cs are available.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Acoustics > Elastic Waves > Elastic Waves, Time Explicit; node eltem1. Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("elte", "ElasticWavesTimeExplicit", "geom1"); physics("elte").feature("eltem1").set("SolidModel", "Anisotropic")

parameters.name: SolidModel
parameters.description: Isotropic | Orthotropic | Anisotropic material symmetry (with TransverseIsotropic and CrystalSystem options).

parameters.name: IsotropicOption
parameters.description: Enu | EG | KG | Lame | CpCs specification of isotropic data.

parameters.name: D / DVo / Dinv, AnisotropicOption
parameters.description: Elasticity or compliance matrix, standard or Voigt ordering.

parameters.name: MaxWaveSpeed, cmax, LFtau, ActivateFilter
parameters.description: Maximum wave speed estimate for the time step, flux parameter and filter.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module (also available with the Structural Mechanics Module). Couples to pressure acoustics time-explicit interfaces with the Acoustic-Structure Boundary, Time Explicit coupling (seismic_waves_earth). Add Material Discontinuity at material interfaces.

tools.name: Low-Reflecting Boundary (Elastic Waves, Time Explicit)
tools.description: Boundary condition that lets elastic P and S waves leave the model with minimal reflection by matching the mechanical impedance of the material (default d = 0.5*rho*(cp+cs) on the diagonal); it is most effective at normal incidence. It is intended to be placed on the outer boundary of Absorbing Layers to form an efficient sponge for all angles, e.g. in seismic and NDT simulations.
tools.usage: Right-click Elastic Waves, Time Explicit > Low-Reflecting Boundary (lrb1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("elte").create("lrb1", "LowReflectingBoundary", 2)

parameters.name: DampingType
parameters.description: PSwaves (from material) | userdef.

parameters.name: d_i
parameters.description: User-defined mechanical impedance (isotropic, diagonal or symmetric).

parameters.name: NormalAxis, coordinateSystem
parameters.description: Axis used as wave direction in a boundary coordinate system.

parameters.name: CalculateDissipatedEnergy
parameters.description: Compute the energy absorbed by the boundary.

tools.notes: Also used in isotropic_anisotropic_sample, angle_beam_ndt, lamb_waves_ndt_plate and flow_meter_piezoelectric_transducers.

tools.name: Fracture (Elastic Waves, Time Explicit)
tools.description: Interior or pair condition that joins two elastic domains with imperfect bonding modeled as distributed springs, representing thin elastic or fluid-filled layers, delaminations, cracks and other defects. It is used in ultrasonic nondestructive testing to simulate the echo from a flaw and in geophysics for fractured media. Stiffness is given per unit area, per unit length, as a total, or from the material data of a thin layer with thickness ds.
tools.usage: Right-click Elastic Waves, Time Explicit > Interior Conditions > Fracture (frac1) or Pairs > Fracture. Java: model.component("comp1").physics("elte").create("frac1", "Fracture", 1)

parameters.name: StiffnessType
parameters.description: kPerArea | kPerLength | kTot | useMatData.

parameters.name: kPerArea, kPerLine, kTot
parameters.description: Spring constants (isotropic, diagonal or symmetric).

parameters.name: ds, E, nu, K, G, IsotropicOption
parameters.description: Layer thickness and elastic data for the material-data option.

parameters.name: TimeSteppingMethod, coordinateSystem
parameters.description: ODE | BackwardEuler update of the fracture displacement; boundary system (sys1) by default.

tools.notes: Zero stiffness gives a traction-free crack; very large stiffness approaches perfect bonding (and reduces the stable time step). Also used in lamb_waves_ndt_plate.

tools.name: Damping and Compute Displacement (Elastic Waves, Time Explicit)
tools.description: Two subnodes of the Elastic Waves, Time Explicit Model. Damping adds Rayleigh (mass- and stiffness-proportional) bulk damping, given as alpha and beta or as damping ratios at two frequencies, and automatically enables filtering for stability; piezoelectric domains use the similar Mechanical Damping. Compute Displacement adds an ODE that integrates the velocity to displacement on selected points, edges, surfaces or domains, needed because the formulation solves for velocity and strain.
tools.usage: Right-click Elastic Waves, Time Explicit Model > Damping (dmp1) / Compute Displacement (cdisp1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("elte").feature("eltem1").create("dmp1", "Damping", 3); feature("eltem1").create("cdisp1", "ComputeDisplacement", 2)

parameters.name: DampingType, InputParameters
parameters.description: Rayleigh damping via alpha/beta or damping ratios.

parameters.name: alpha_dM, beta_dK
parameters.description: Mass and stiffness damping parameters.

parameters.name: f1, f2, zeta1, zeta2
parameters.description: Frequencies and damping ratios for the damping-ratio input.

parameters.name: AttenuationUnit, alphap_dBm, alphas_dBm (Mechanical Damping)
parameters.description: Attenuation of P and S waves in dB/m or Np/m for piezo materials.

tools.notes: Compute Displacement is postprocessing only and costs extra DOFs; restrict it to where needed.

tools.name: Piezoelectric Waves, Time Explicit (multiphysics interface)
tools.description: Predefined multiphysics interface combining Elastic Waves, Time Explicit and Electrostatics with a Piezoelectric Material node and the Piezoelectricity, Time Explicit coupling, for transient piezoelectric wave propagation (direct and inverse effect) in stress-charge or strain-charge form. The elastic waves use dG with explicit time stepping while electrostatics is solved by FEM at every time step; used for ultrasonic transducers in NDT and flowmeters.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Acoustics > Elastic Waves > Piezoelectric Waves, Time Explicit (adds elte + es + pzete1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("elte").create("pzm1", "PiezoelectricMaterialModel", 2); model.component("comp1").multiphysics().create("pzete1", "PiezoelectricEffectTimeExplicit", 2)

parameters.name: ConstitutiveRelation
parameters.description: StressCharge | StrainCharge.

parameters.name: cE, eES, epsilonrS / sE, dET, epsilonrT
parameters.description: Elasticity, coupling and permittivity matrices (stress-charge) or compliance form (strain-charge).

parameters.name: coordinateSystem
parameters.description: Polarization orientation of the crystal.

parameters.name: MaxWaveSpeed, cmax, ActivateFilter
parameters.description: Time step control and filtering.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics, Structural Mechanics or MEMS Module. Without the coupling the Piezoelectric Material behaves as purely elastic.

tools.name: Poroelastic Material (Poroelastic Waves)
tools.description: Domain node of the Poroelastic Waves interface defining an isotropic porous material by its drained elastic skeleton and saturating fluid, solved with Biot's mixed u-p formulation. Models: Biot (viscous losses, for water/oil-saturated rocks and soils) and Biot-Allard (default; viscous and thermal losses via JCA, for air-saturated foams, fibers and liners). Fast and slow pressure waves and shear waves propagate; their speeds are pelw.cp_fast, pelw.cp_slow and pelw.cs_poro.
tools.usage: Poroelastic Waves > Poroelastic Material 1 (pm1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("pelw").feature("pm1").set("PoroelasticModel", "BiotAllard")

parameters.name: PoroelasticModel
parameters.description: Biot | BiotAllard.

parameters.name: E, nu (IsotropicOption), rhod, eta_s
parameters.description: Drained skeleton elasticity, drained density and structural loss factor.

parameters.name: epsilon_p, Rf, tau, Lv, Lth, kappa_p
parameters.description: Porosity, flow resistivity, tortuosity, characteristic lengths, permeability.

parameters.name: alphaB, Ks, ViscosityModel, fr, a
parameters.description: Biot-Willis coefficient, grain bulk modulus, Biot low/high-frequency viscosity model, reference frequency or pore size.

parameters.name: rhof, muf, chif (or FluidMaterial)
parameters.description: Saturating fluid density, viscosity and compressibility.

tools.notes: The interface type string is PoroelasticWavesSinglePhysics (tag pelw). Mesh must resolve the slow wave; see 'Meshing Poroelastic Waves Models'.

tools.name: Anisotropic Poroelastic Material (Poroelastic Waves)
tools.description: Poroelastic material model with anisotropic skeleton elasticity and direction-dependent porous properties (flow resistivity, tortuosity, characteristic lengths, permeability) in a local coordinate system, solved with Biot or Biot-Allard theory. It is used for fibrous, layered or transversely isotropic absorbers and anisotropic rocks.
tools.usage: Right-click Poroelastic Waves > Anisotropic Poroelastic Material (apm1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("pelw").create("apm1", "AnisotropicPoroelasticWavesMaterial", 3)

parameters.name: coordinateSystem
parameters.description: Local material axes.

parameters.name: D / DVo, AnisotropicOption / OrthotropicOption
parameters.description: Drained elasticity matrix (standard or Voigt ordering) or orthotropic data.

parameters.name: Rf, tau, Lv (tensors), epsilon_p, Lth
parameters.description: Anisotropic and scalar porous parameters.

parameters.name: DampingType
parameters.description: Skeleton damping model.

tools.notes: Also used in anisotropic_porous_absorber. For a rigid anisotropic frame the cheaper Anisotropic Poroacoustics in pressure acoustics may suffice.

tools.name: Impervious Layer / Impervious Mass Layer / Free, Sound Soft (Poroelastic Waves)
tools.description: Boundary conditions of the Poroelastic Waves interface acting on the pore fluid and/or skeleton. Impervious Layer (a default) is sound hard for the pore-fluid pressure and combines with any porous-matrix condition (Free, Fixed Constraint, Roller, loads). Impervious Mass Layer adds a distributed mass (e.g. a film or facing) on the skeleton with an impervious fluid condition. Free, Sound Soft leaves the matrix unloaded and sets zero pore pressure; Interior Impervious Layer and Thin Elastic Layer handle interior boundaries.
tools.usage: Right-click Poroelastic Waves > Fluid Conditions / Porous Matrix Conditions. Java: model.component("comp1").physics("pelw").create("il2", "ImperviousLayer", 2); create("iml1", "ImperviousMassLayer", 2); create("pfree1", "PorousFree", 2)

parameters.name: MassType, mPerArea, mPerLine, mTot (Impervious Mass Layer)
parameters.description: Added mass per area, per length or total, isotropic/diagonal/symmetric.

parameters.name: Spring type (Thin Elastic Layer)
parameters.description: Elastic and damping properties between two parts.

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Boundaries of the porous domain.

tools.notes: Couple to air with the Acoustic-Porous Boundary and to solids with the Porous-Structure Boundary multiphysics couplings rather than with these conditions.

tools.name: Solid Mechanics (Elastic Waves) shortcut interface
tools.description: Entry under Acoustics > Elastic Waves that adds a standard Solid Mechanics interface configured for elastic wave problems solved with the dynamic Navier equation in the frequency domain, with default Linear Elastic Material, Free and Initial Values. It is the FEM route for vibroacoustics, scattered elastic waves (Background Elastic Wave formulation) and elastic cloaks, and couples to pressure acoustics, poroelastic and thermoviscous domains through the acoustics multiphysics couplings.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Acoustics > Elastic Waves > Solid Mechanics (Elastic Waves). Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("solid", "SolidMechanics", "geom1")

parameters.name: Linear Elastic Material
parameters.description: Isotropic/anisotropic elasticity and damping (loss factor, Rayleigh).

parameters.name: Low-Reflecting Boundary / PML
parameters.description: Open-boundary treatment for elastic waves in the frequency domain.

parameters.name: Meshing
parameters.description: Resolve the shear wavelength, typically the shortest, with 5-6 second-order elements.

tools.notes: Features are documented in the Structural Mechanics/COMSOL Multiphysics manuals. For transient wave propagation over many wavelengths use Elastic Waves, Time Explicit.

tools.name: Pipe Properties (Pipe Acoustics)
tools.description: Edge node of the Pipe Acoustics interfaces defining the pipe cross section (round, square, rectangular or user-defined area and wetted perimeter) and the pipe wall model that sets the effective wave speed: incompressible cross section, zero axial stress, anchored at one end or anchored at both ends (using E, nu and wall thickness). It also sets wall friction and the flow profile correction factor for the 1D plane-wave pipe equations.
tools.usage: Pipe Acoustics, Frequency Domain (or Transient) > Pipe Properties 1 (pipe1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("pafd").feature("pipe1").set("shape", "Round")

parameters.name: shape
parameters.description: NotSet | Round | Square | Rectangular | UserDefined.

parameters.name: innerd, innerw, innerh, A, Z
parameters.description: Inner diameter, width, height or area and wetted perimeter.

parameters.name: pipeModel
parameters.description: IncompressibleCrossSection | ZeroAxialStress | AnchoredAtOneEnd | AnchoredAtBothEnds.

parameters.name: E, nu, dw, PipeMaterial
parameters.description: Wall elasticity and thickness for compliant pipes.

parameters.name: tauw, beta
parameters.description: Wall friction and flow profile correction factor.

tools.notes: The Pipe Acoustics interface type strings are FrequencyPipeAcoustics (pafd) and TransientPipeAcoustics (patd). The effective wave speed can be evaluated as sqrt(1/pafd.invc2). Only plane waves are modeled; check the cutoff frequency of higher modes.

tools.name: End Impedance (Pipe Acoustics)
tools.description: Point condition at the end of a 1D pipe giving the termination impedance: an infinite pipe (characteristic impedance, nonreflecting; low-Mach limit or general), the radiation impedance of a flanged (baffled) circular or rectangular pipe, an unflanged circular pipe (low ka approximation or full model), or a user-defined impedance from measurements. Used for open ends of organ pipes, ventilation outlets and exhaust tailpipes.
tools.usage: Right-click Pipe Acoustics > End Impedance (endimp1) on a point. Java: model.component("comp1").physics("pafd").create("endimp1", "EndImpedance", 0)

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description: InfinitePipeLowMa | InfinitePipe | FlangedPipeCircular | FlangedPipeRectangular | UnflangedPipeCircularLowka | UnflangedPipeCircular | UserDefined (transient: infinite pipe or user defined).

parameters.name: innera, innerw, innerh, k
parameters.description: Pipe radius or width/height and wave number for radiation impedances.

parameters.name: Zend
parameters.description: User-defined end impedance (default rho*c).

tools.notes: Couple a pipe end to a 3D pressure acoustics domain with the Acoustic-Pipe Acoustic Connection multiphysics coupling instead (no-flow case).

tools.name: Fluid Properties, Velocity, Pressure and Closed (Pipe Acoustics)
tools.description: Remaining nodes of the 1D Pipe Acoustics interfaces. Fluid Properties (default edge node) defines the momentum and continuity equations, the fluid density and free-space speed of sound and an optional background mean flow velocity u0 with pressure/temperature model inputs (u0 and p0 can come from a Pipe Flow solution). Point conditions: Velocity (inlet velocity source), Pressure (boundary pressure source) and Closed (rigid end); Volume Force adds a distributed axial force.
tools.usage: Pipe Acoustics > Fluid Properties 1 (fp1, default); right-click > Velocity (source1) / Pressure (pres1) / Closed (closed1) / Volume Force (vf1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("pafd").create("pres1", "Pressure", 0); create("source1", "Source", 0); create("closed1", "Closed", 0)

parameters.name: rho, cs, u0, fluidmodel (Fluid Properties)
parameters.description: Density, free-space speed of sound, background mean flow velocity, LinearElastic fluid model.

parameters.name: uin (Velocity)
parameters.description: Inlet velocity amplitude.

parameters.name: p (Pressure)
parameters.description: Boundary pressure amplitude.

parameters.name: F (Volume Force)
parameters.description: Axial volume force.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module or the Pipe Flow Module. SPL along the pipe is pafd.Lp. The transient interface uses the same node types.
